plan.title: Explore dataset structure and statistics
plan.description: Write scratch.py to load annotations.json and metadata.json. Print: number of images, annotations, categories, annotation distribution per image (min/max/mean/median), category frequency distribution, how many categories have <5 annotations, image sizes, and verify file paths exist for a sample of train images and product reference images. Also check which product_codes in annotations have matching folders in data/products/.
plan.success_criteria: Complete statistical summary of the dataset logged, understanding of class distribution and data linkage

plan.title: Verify environment and available tools
plan.description: Write scratch.py to check: ultralytics version, torch version, CUDA availability, GPU memory, available disk space. Also test that we can load a pretrained YOLOv8 model (e.g., yolov8n.pt) and run inference on a single image. Check what pretrained weights are available locally or bundled with ultralytics 8.1.0.
plan.success_criteria: Confirmed GPU access, ultralytics working, know which pretrained models are available

plan.title: Detection-only baseline with YOLOv8n at 640px
plan.hypothesis: A YOLOv8n model fine-tuned for single-class detection at 640px for ~30 epochs can achieve detection_mAP@0.5 > 0.5, giving final_score > 0.35
plan.description: Convert COCO annotations to YOLO format with all categories mapped to class 0 (single-class detection). Split data 90/10 train/val. Train YOLOv8n at imgsz=640 for 30 epochs. Evaluate detection mAP@0.5 on val set. Build submission with all predictions as category_id=0. Use main.py for training and model export.

plan.title: Detection-only with YOLOv8m at 1280px
plan.hypothesis: Larger model (YOLOv8m) and higher resolution (1280px) significantly improve detection on dense shelves, achieving detection_mAP@0.5 > 0.70
plan.description: Train YOLOv8m single-class detection at imgsz=1280 for 50 epochs with the same train/val split. Use appropriate batch size for A100 80GB. Compare against step 3 baseline.

plan.title: Detection with YOLOv8l/x at 1280px with augmentation tuning
plan.hypothesis: YOLOv8l or YOLOv8x with tuned augmentation (mosaic, mixup, copy-paste) further improves dense detection
plan.description: Train YOLOv8l at 1280px for 80 epochs. Tune augmentation parameters: reduce mosaic probability (dense scenes may not benefit), add copy-paste augmentation, adjust scale/translate. Use cosine LR schedule.

plan.title: Multi-class detection with YOLOv8m
plan.hypothesis: Training with all 357 categories enables both detection and classification, potentially achieving final_score > 0.50 (0.7*det + 0.3*cls)
plan.description: Convert annotations to YOLO format preserving all category_ids. Train YOLOv8m at 1280px for 80 epochs with all 357 classes. Evaluate both detection mAP and classification mAP. Compare final_score against detection-only approach.

plan.title: SAHI (Sliced Inference) for dense small objects
plan.hypothesis: Slicing high-res images into overlapping tiles during inference improves detection of small/dense products
plan.description: Take the best detection model from steps 4-5. Implement sliced inference: divide each test image into overlapping 640x640 or 1280x1280 tiles, run detection on each tile, merge with NMS/WBF. Compare against full-image inference.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improves by >2% over full-image inference

plan.title: Two-stage approach: detect then classify with crop-based classifier
plan.hypothesis: Detecting products first (single-class), then classifying crops with a separate classifier achieves better classification than end-to-end multi-class detection
plan.description: Use best single-class detector to extract product crops from training images. Train a classification model (ResNet50 or EfficientNet via timm) on these crops with 357 classes. At inference: detect → crop → classify. Include product reference images as additional training data for the classifier.
plan.success_criteria: classification accuracy on val crops > 40%, final_score > detection-only score

plan.title: Reference image matching with DINOv2 embeddings
plan.hypothesis: Using DINOv2 features to match detected crops against product reference images achieves better classification than a trained classifier, especially for rare classes
plan.description: Extract DINOv2 (via timm) embeddings for all product reference images (main.jpg, front.jpg). Build a reference gallery. For each detected crop, extract embedding and find nearest neighbor. Evaluate classification accuracy. Try both global features and patch-level matching.
plan.success_criteria: Top-1 retrieval accuracy > 35% on val crops, competitive with or better than trained classifier

plan.title: Combine classifier and retrieval for classification
plan.hypothesis: Ensembling trained classifier scores with retrieval similarity scores improves classification over either alone
plan.description: For each detected crop, get probability distribution from trained classifier (step 8) and similarity scores from DINOv2 retrieval (step 9). Combine with weighted average or learned fusion. Evaluate on val set.

plan.title: Multi-scale detection ensemble with WBF
plan.hypothesis: Ensembling detections from multiple model sizes and input resolutions with Weighted Boxes Fusion improves detection mAP
plan.description: Run inference with YOLOv8m@1280, YOLOv8l@1280, and YOLOv8m@1600 (or SAHI). Merge predictions using ensemble_boxes WBF. Tune IoU threshold and confidence weights.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improves by >1.5% over best single model

plan.title: RT-DETR as alternative detector
plan.hypothesis: RT-DETR (transformer-based detector available in ultralytics) may handle dense scenes differently and complement YOLO in an ensemble
plan.description: Train RT-DETR-l from ultralytics at 1280px for single-class detection. Compare against best YOLO model. If competitive, add to ensemble from step 11.
plan.success_criteria: RT-DETR detection_mAP@0.5 within 3% of best YOLO model

plan.title: Optimize inference pipeline for 300s timeout
plan.hypothesis: The full pipeline (detection + classification) can run within 300s on L4 GPU with ONNX optimization
plan.description: Profile the full inference pipeline. Export detection model to ONNX. Optimize classification/retrieval to batch process crops efficiently. Ensure total inference on ~60 test images completes within 300s. Consider FP16 inference.
plan.success_criteria: Full pipeline completes inference on 248 images in <300s on L4 GPU

plan.title: Synthetic training data from reference images
plan.hypothesis: Pasting product reference images onto shelf backgrounds as synthetic training data improves classification for rare classes
plan.description: For categories with <5 training annotations, generate synthetic training images by pasting reference product images onto random shelf backgrounds with augmentation (rotation, scale, lighting). Add these to training set and retrain classifier.
plan.success_criteria: Classification accuracy on rare classes (annotation_count < 5) improves by >10%

plan.title: Test-time augmentation for detection
plan.hypothesis: TTA (horizontal flip, multi-scale) improves detection mAP by capturing products at different scales
plan.description: Implement TTA for the best detection model: run inference at multiple scales (1024, 1280, 1536) and with horizontal flip. Merge with WBF. Measure improvement and time cost.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improves by >1% while staying within time budget

plan.title: Final submission assembly and optimization
plan.hypothesis: Combining best detection ensemble with best classification approach maximizes final_score
plan.description: Assemble the complete pipeline: best detection method (ensemble/SAHI/TTA) + best classification method (classifier + retrieval fusion). Tune confidence thresholds for detection and classification separately. Generate final submission. Ensure everything fits in 420MB and runs in 300s.
